source: Li & Kingsford (2026) Means-ends analysis for LLM planning (MEDAKA, LiquidWorld) - ablation
finding: Full ablation re-read. Removing state tracking or the recursive module each costs a few points for Claude and more for Gemini, mostly on nonlinear, coupling and multi-goal tags. There is NO ablation of operator choice by gap size, and NO discrete-domain test (no Blocksworld or Hanoi runs).
numbers: Total pass@1: Claude-Sonnet-4.6 94.5 full, 90.5 no state tracking, 91.0 no recursion. Gemini-3-Flash 82.0, 76.0, 75.1. Nonlinear tag Gemini 50.9 / 36.5 / 28.9; multi-goal Gemini 60.5 / 46.9 / 43.4; linear Gemini 94.1 / 91.4 / 93.1. 189 problems, 3 rollouts, temperature 0. Authors note the two parts need not add up.
limits: Single group, synthetic water-vessel tasks, no operator-selection ablation. Gap 4 is answered only as untested: recursion and state tracking matter on hard tags, operator choice is unknown.
agent_relevance: Keep state tracking and recursion in O5; do not claim gap-size operator choice is what helps until we ablate it.

source: Li & Kingsford (2026) MEDAKA - token cost and pass@3 parity
finding: MEDAKA costs 1.8x to 3.8x the tokens of plain CoT. The authors compare with CoT pass@3 for compute parity. MEDAKA pass@1 beats CoT pass@3 on 4 of 7 models, not on GPT-5.4 or the two Gemma4 models.
numbers: Median total tokens per trial: Claude CoT 2185 vs MEDAKA 6857 (3.1x); Gemini 1989 vs 4053 (2.0x); GPT-5.4 1859 vs 7013 (3.8x); GPT-4o 1849 vs 4402. Pass@3 totals: Claude CoT 86.8, AoT+ 95.2, MEDAKA 97.9; Gemini 67.2 / 72.0 / 84.1; GPT-5.4 82.0 / 88.9 / 89.4. At about 3 CoT samples the MEDAKA pass@3 lead is +11.1 for Claude and +16.9 for Gemini, but only +7.4 for GPT-5.4 over CoT and +0.5 over AoT+.
limits: Pass@3 is an any-of-3 metric, so it flatters resampling; a real equal-token test would use majority vote. Not a true equal-token test.
agent_relevance: The beats-resampling claim holds for non-reasoning models only; run our own equal-token comparison.

source: Li & Kingsford (2026) MEDAKA - GPT-5.4 and thinking mode
finding: Thinking mode was disabled for all models on purpose. So the paper never tests whether MEA helps on top of long native reasoning. GPT-5.4 tied AoT+ at 78.5 and lost to AoT+ on nonlinear and distractor tags.
numbers: GPT-5.4 pass@1 by tag CoT / AoT+ / MEDAKA: linear 91.9/90.0/90.9; nonlinear 28.9/49.1/46.5; coupling 54.7/62.9/62.9; multi-goal 43.4/56.6/54.8; distractor 72.6/83.3/76.2. Totals 74.3 / 78.5 / 78.5.
limits: Gap 1 stays open: no run with thinking on vs off at equal tokens exists. The GPT-5.4 numbers are the closest evidence and point to little gain.
agent_relevance: Treat gap-driven prompting as a scaffold for non-thinking calls; test on/off before keeping it for thinking calls.

source: Meincke, Mollick, Mollick, Shapiro (2025) Prompting Science Report 2: The Decreasing Value of Chain of Thought in Prompting
finding: Asking for step-by-step reasoning adds little for reasoning models and helps non-reasoning models only a bit, while costing more time. It can lower the share of questions answered correctly every time.
numbers: GPQA Diamond, 198 questions x 25 trials = 4,950 runs per prompt per model. Non-reasoning, step-by-step vs direct (average rating): Gemini Flash 2.0 +13.5 points, Sonnet 3.5 +11.7, GPT-4o-mini +4.4 (ns). Versus default behaviour: Gemini Flash 2.0 +6.2, GPT-4o +6.9, Sonnet 3.5 -1.9 (ns), GPT-4o-mini +0.4 (ns). Reasoning models vs direct: o3-mini +2.9, o4-mini +3.1, Gemini Flash 2.5 -3.3 (all p<.05); Flash 2.5 100%-correct metric fell 13.1 points. CoT added 35-600% time for non-reasoning and 20-80% for reasoning models.
limits: Generic CoT on multiple-choice science questions, not a structured planning scaffold. Indirect support for gap 1.
agent_relevance: Structured scaffolds on top of native reasoning will probably have a small and possibly negative effect; measure it, do not assume.

source: Shojaee et al. (2025) The Illusion of Thinking - thinking vs non-thinking at equal token compute
finding: On puzzle environments including Hanoi and Blocksworld, thinking and non-thinking pairs behave in three regimes at matched inference tokens: non-thinking models are as good or better at low complexity, thinking models win at medium complexity, and both collapse at high complexity.
numbers: Pairs: Claude 3.7 Sonnet thinking vs non-thinking, DeepSeek-R1 vs V3; 64k token cap for Claude. Pass@k compared across equivalent compute budgets.
limits: Evaluation artefacts disputed (see d20). Text read from the preprint PDF.
agent_relevance: A scaffold that adds tokens helps in the middle range only; for easy steps it wastes tokens, for very hard ones it does not rescue.

source: Vollmeyer, Burns & Holyoak (1996) The impact of goal specificity on strategy use and the acquisition of problem structure. Cognitive Science 20(1):75-100
finding: Answers the Vollmeyer part of gap 3 in words: the cost of a specific goal runs through strategy. Without a specific goal people test hypotheses more systematically; a specific goal pushes difference reduction, which teaches one solution path, not the structure. Instruction in systematic rule induction helped with either goal type, but people used it less when the goal was specific.
numbers: Two experiments on a complex dynamic system. Specific-goal group did well on the first problem and worse on a transfer problem with a different goal. No group means or N were available to me.
limits: Only abstract and reference list read (full text blocked, 403). Numbers still missing.
agent_relevance: Goal-free benefit is mediated by systematic hypothesis testing. For our agent: require explicit hypothesis tests, not just removing the goal.

source: Sweller (1988) Cognitive load during problem solving: effects on learning. Cognitive Science 12(2):257-285
finding: Abstract: means-ends analysis needs much processing capacity that is then not available for schema acquisition; a computational model and experiments support this.
numbers: No numbers available (abstract only via Crossref).
quote: conventional problem solving in the form of means-ends analysis requires a relatively large amount of cognitive processing capacity
limits: Abstract only; PDF blocked. Cognitive-load account, competing with Vollmeyer's strategy account.
agent_relevance: MEA competes with learning for working memory; in an agent, long gap bookkeeping may crowd out useful reasoning.

source: Learning goal-free problems: collaboratively or individually? (2019) Jurnal Cakrawala Pendidikan 38(3)
finding: A classroom replication of the goal-free effect in geometry: goal-free learners had higher far-transfer scores but higher cognitive load during acquisition, and individuals beat collaborative pairs on far transfer.
numbers: N=111 seventh graders; 2 (goal-free vs goal-given) x 2 (collaborative vs individual) design; effect sizes not in the abstract.
limits: Abstract only; low-visibility journal; the higher load during acquisition conflicts with the pure load-reduction story.
agent_relevance: Supports goal-free benefit for far transfer but not as a load saver.

source: Citation records for Sweller & Levine (1982, JEP:LMC 8(5):463), Owen & Sweller (1985, J Educ Psych 77(3):272), Ayres (1993, Contemp Educ Psych), Atwood & Polson (1976), Kotovsky et al. (1985)
finding: Existence and titles confirmed through Crossref only. Abstracts and numbers (effect sizes, N, boundary conditions) could NOT be obtained; publisher sites returned 403 and search quotas were exhausted.
numbers: None.
limits: Not opened. Do not quote effect sizes from these papers until a copy is read.
agent_relevance: Gap 3 numbers remain open.

source: Meyerson et al. (2025) Solving a Million-Step LLM Task with Zero Errors (MAKER)
finding: Per-step voting works for a rigid step type (one Hanoi move) with a cheap non-reasoning model. The paper has no equal-compute comparison against a bigger reasoning budget and no no-voting baseline run.
numbers: Single-step error: gpt-4.1-mini 0.0022 (k_min 3, $3.5K projected); o3-mini low 0.0018 (k_min 3, $9.4K); haiku-4.5 0.1839 (k_min 12, $71.2K); gpt-4.1-nano 0.3571 ($41.9K); gpt-oss-20B 0.0358 ($1.7K). Responses over about 700 tokens go wrong much more often (red-flag cutoff 750 tokens). Steps: 1,048,575. No per-step-type breakdown.
limits: Projected costs, one task type.
agent_relevance: Voting is a cheap fix only for short, checkable, repeated steps; the reasoning model cost more at the same error rate here.

source: Singhi et al. (2025) When To Solve, When To Verify: compute-optimal problem solving and generative verification
finding: At equal inference compute (verification cost counted) majority-vote self-consistency beats generative verification at most practical budgets. Verification pays only at large budgets and on harder problems.
numbers: Llama-3.1-8B on MATH (128 problems): GenRM matches SC at about 8x SC's compute and beats it only at about 128x, by 3.8%. QwQ-32B on AIME 2025: matches at 4x, +2.5% at 16x. LiveCodeBench: matches at 16x, +3.5% at 64x. MATH Level 5 gain up to about 30% relative. Solutions should scale about 1.5-2x faster than verifications.
limits: Learned/LLM verifier on math, not an exact checker; small test sets (64-128 problems).
agent_relevance: Gap 6 (LLM-verifier half): do not add soft per-step verification by default; spend on more samples. Exact external checkers (d13, d14) are a different case.

source: Snell et al. (2024) Scaling LLM test-time compute optimally can be more effective than scaling model parameters
finding: Adaptive allocation by prompt difficulty beats uniform best-of-N; revision and verifier search each win in different difficulty bands.
numbers: More than 4x efficiency over best-of-N; a smaller base model beat a 14x larger one in a FLOPs-matched comparison, only where the small model had non-trivial success.
limits: Math tasks; abstract only.
agent_relevance: Allocate gap-driven or voting effort per step by estimated difficulty.

source: Kambhampati et al. (2024) LLMs Can't Plan, But Can Help Planning in LLM-Modulo Frameworks
finding: An exact external verifier with back-prompting lifts planning a lot on plain domains and little on obfuscated ones. Compute is not matched against a larger reasoning budget.
numbers: Blocksworld 82% within 15 rounds, Logistics 70%, Mystery Blocksworld about 10%; travel planning about 6x baselines (10 cycles). Direct GPT-4: Blocksworld 206/600 (34.3%) one-shot, 210/600 (34.6%) zero-shot; Mystery 26/600 (4.3%) one-shot.
limits: No equal-compute comparison, no critic ablation in the text read.
agent_relevance: Exact validators on step results are worth the tokens; do not copy this result to soft self-critique.

source: Valmeekam, Stechly, Kambhampati (2024) LLMs still can't plan; can LRMs? o1 on PlanBench
finding: Reasoning model o1-preview jumps on plain and obfuscated Blocksworld but costs far more, drops with obfuscation, and still fails at larger sizes. An external verifier loop on top of o1 gives big gains at higher cost.
numbers: Blocksworld 3-5 blocks zero-shot: o1-preview 97.8%, o1-mini 56.6%. Mystery zero-shot: 52.8% / 19.1%. Randomized Mystery: 37.3% / 3.5%. 6-20 block Blocksworld: o1-preview 23.63% (text) vs 23.65% (table). Unsolvable cases flagged: 27%. Cost per 100 instances: o1-preview $42.12, GPT-4o $0.65, GPT-4 $1.80. LRM-Modulo hard Blocksworld: 23.65% ($52.12) to 98.2% (7 iterations, $139.36); o1-mini 0.9% to 10%; Sokoban 12.7% to 43.6%. Reasoning-token use did not track nodes expanded.
limits: Single research group; reasoning token counts not given; Fast Downward 100% at 0.12 s.
agent_relevance: Gap 6 evidence: verifier loop gave +74.6 points at about 2.7x cost on o1-preview, so exact verification beats raising budget for hard multi-step planning.

source: Valmeekam et al. (2023) On the planning abilities of LLMs - a critical investigation
finding: Records the version-specific PlanBench numbers and shows that obfuscating names kills GPT-4's plan success. Even under the most lenient plan checking, many Blocksworld plans miss the goal. No study of goal ordering or protecting achieved goals is reported (instances only vary subgoal interaction type).
numbers: GPT-4 one-shot: Blocksworld 206/600 (34.3%), CoT 214/600 (35.6%), Mystery deceptive 26/600 (4.3%) one-shot, 1/600 zero-shot, CoT 54/600 (9%), randomized 12/600 (2%). Instruct-GPT3 deceptive one-shot 14/600 printed as 2.3% in this version. About 39% of GPT-4 Blocksworld plans still failed the goal under delete+precondition relaxation. VAL backprompt: 41/50, 35/50, 5/50. Human baseline 39/50 (78%), 35 of 39 optimal. Human-in-loop: 49 unassisted vs 48 LLM-assisted, accuracy p=0.22.
limits: The 0.23% typo noted by the cross-checker is not in this version; it may be in another. Versions differ.
agent_relevance: Renamed symbols collapse plain-model performance: our agent's gap logic must be tested on renamed domains.

source: Prasad et al. (2024) ADaPT: As-Needed Decomposition and Planning (re-read)
finding: Re-read: no always-decompose ablation and no token or dollar cost; calls are only shown in a figure and are said to be comparable to Try-Again and Reflexion. Self-assessed success is unreliable on WebShop. Single run per model.
numbers: GPT-3.5: ALFWorld 71.6 vs ReAct 43.3, Plan-and-Execute 43.3, Reflexion 57.5; WebShop 44.0 vs 32.0, 17.0, 35.0; TextCraft 52.0 vs 19.0, 27.0, 32.0. TextCraft recipe depth 3: ReAct 1.8 vs ADaPT 38.7. d_max 1 equals ReAct. WebShop self-assessed success inflated by more than 30 points.
limits: No independent replication found in this session (search quota exhausted). Gap 8 stays open.
agent_relevance: Decompose on failure only; but we have no measured token overhead.

source: Katz et al. (2024) Thought of Search: planning with language models through the lens of efficiency
finding: Have the LLM write the successor and goal-test code once, then run ordinary BFS/DFS. This reaches 100% on 24 Game, mini crosswords, BlocksWorld and PrOntoQA with a few LLM calls.
numbers: Measured model interactions: about 2.2 (24 Game), 3.8 (BlocksWorld). Projected calls for BlocksWorld: CoT 502, ToT 201K, RAP 482K, LATS 562K. Estimated cost about $14,000 for RAP and $16,000 for LATS vs about $40 for CoT. BlocksWorld 4-5 blocks, GPT-4 only.
limits: Human validates the code; small instances; cost estimates assume 500 input and 50 output tokens per call.
agent_relevance: For discrete domains with a checkable rule set, writing operator code beats per-step LLM search; relevant to O5 operator choice.

source: Wu et al. (2023) Reasoning or Reciting? Counterfactual tasks
finding: Models do worse on counterfactual variants of tasks they do well on by default, but the two are correlated, so it is a mix of reciting and transferable reasoning.
numbers: GPT-3.5 parseable programs 99% default vs 62% (vertical flip), 71% (90 degree), 75% (180 degree). Arithmetic: near-perfect to near-zero in some bases. Models GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Claude v1.3, PaLM-2. Zero-shot CoT usually helps but hurts PaLM-2 base-10/16 addition.
limits: Exact default-vs-counterfactual scores sit in figures not read. No Hanoi or Blocksworld.
agent_relevance: Gap 7: use renamed-symbol variants as a standing control for every scaffold test.

source: Donnarumma, Maisto, Pezzulo (2016) Problem solving as probabilistic inference with subgoaling: Tower of Hanoi. PLoS Comput Biol
finding: Primary source for the bottleneck result: with two shortest routes, people chose the one-bottleneck route in 72% of cases; the subgoaling model reproduces 72% after four voting iterations. Most particles on the optimal plan used 2 or 3 subgoals.
numbers: 72% (human); simulation 72%; 25 runs per model in simulations. Human participant counts not given in the text read (patient/control data are from earlier work).
limits: Model is a particle-based inference, not a rule tested on LLMs. Gap 9 (LLM test of a bottleneck rule) stays open.
agent_relevance: Rule to try: prefer the plan with fewest bottleneck crossings when proposing subgoals; untested for LLMs.

source: Lawsen (2025) The Illusion of the Illusion of Thinking (re-read)
finding: Hanoi collapse reproduced as an output-length effect: asking for a function gives high accuracy in under 5,000 tokens at N=15; some River Crossing cases are unsolvable and were scored wrong.
numbers: Models Claude-3.7-Sonnet, Claude Opus 4, o3, Gemini 2.5; N=15; about 10 tokens per move; max N about 12-13 at 64k tokens. River Crossing N>=6 with boat capacity 3 is unsolvable.
limits: Small, preliminary, no exact accuracies or token counts; claim of deliberate truncation rests on a social-media replication.
agent_relevance: Tell the agent to emit a procedure, not a long move list, for long tasks.
